continuation.phase: project-brain ownership and host project-scope integration
continuation.objective: Give Bounded Agent Harness its own portable Project Brain, prevent project checkpoint reuse across projects, and make project-scoped context selection an enforced host boundary.
continuation.last_completed: Published the exact 35-file static BAH candidate from source commit 0150713fcd92629dc0501b9550a8f31b2f414f27 as Netlify deploy 6abb266397e11d601df00913. Netlify reports ready with zero available, required, or edge functions. All 34 publicly served files match the preserved candidate ZIP; `_headers` is control metadata. GitHub exposes the exact source commit. The false access blocker was traced to a local origin pointing at a sibling checkout, sandbox-owned older checkouts, and a missing bundled Git helper path during push; the saved Git credential route remained valid. OPERATOR-GUIDE.md now requires those checks before asking the owner to reconnect anything.
continuation.next_step: Implement the existing planned host-neutral retrieval/injection adapter so project-scoped context selection is enforced before model context construction. Reuse the current project-scope gate and source materializer; do not add a parallel scope engine or deploy a site for this local step.
continuation.resume_command: From the BAH repository root, read PROJECT-BRAIN/README.md, PROJECT-BRAIN/CURRENT-STATE.md, and PROJECT-BRAIN/NEXT-STEP.md. Preserve the work/ artifacts. Confirm the repository identity is bounded-agent-harness, then implement and test the host-neutral retrieval/injection adapter described in NEXT-STEP.md. For any future Git publication, inspect the remote URL and ownership first; on this bundled Windows runtime set GIT_EXEC_PATH from `git --exec-path` for the push process and dry-run before asking the owner to reconnect GitHub.
do_not_repeat: Do not put USB, DFW Metro, FreeVibeApps, or game-project current state into the BAH Project Brain.
Do not copy USB product purpose or private owner history; use only the exact USB evidence pointer declared in PROJECT-BRAIN/PROJECT.json when a BAH claim requires it.
Do not publish private HITL Removal or Danger Mode specifications, credentials, or owner records in this public repository.
Do not treat a GitHub connector 403 or empty plugin repository list as proof that the authenticated Git CLI route is unavailable.
Do not ask the owner to reconnect GitHub before checking the actual remote, checkout ownership, `git --exec-path`, and an explicit HTTPS push dry run.

Do not run `pnpm install --offline` in an isolated worktree; the available store lacks the Next.js 16.2.6 tarball. Do not build from a worktree inside website/work or with a node_modules junction in the site tree.
Use `node --test 'test/*.test.mjs'` for the BAH tracked suite while preserved worktrees live under `work/`; bare `node --test` also discovers their tests and can report unrelated junction failures.
The live site is bound to source commit 0150713fcd92629dc0501b9550a8f31b2f414f27 and deploy 6abb266397e11d601df00913; do not replace it without a separate publication GO.

live.effect_boundary: Production publication of the exact static BAH candidate from source commit 0150713fcd92629dc0501b9550a8f31b2f414f27: zero available/required/edge functions; all 34 public files matched the preserved ZIP; /release.json bound the candidate commit and website digest. No other site, DNS, database, payment, credential, or provider setting changed.

known_problems.summary: The checkout's origin pointed to a sibling local repository, older checkouts had sandbox ownership, and push could not find remote-https until GIT_EXEC_PATH was supplied from git --exec-path. The GitHub plugin exposed zero installed repositories, but the saved Git credential route remained valid and published the exact branch.
known_problems.next_action: For future pushes, verify the canonical remote and checkout ownership, supply the bundled helper path to the push process, perform an explicit HTTPS dry run, and only then diagnose credentials. Follow OPERATOR-GUIDE.md.

known_problems.scope: Node test discovery with preserved worktrees
known_problems.summary: Bare `node --test` recursively discovered tests inside preserved worktrees under `work/`, including failed junction experiments. Those are unrelated to the main BAH test result; the explicit tracked test glob passes 170 tests with one host skip and zero failures.
known_problems.next_action: While these preservation worktrees remain, use `node --test 'test/*.test.mjs'` for exact BAH verification. Do not delete preserved worktrees just to change test discovery.

known_problems.summary: The gate and file-backed materializer are proven locally, but no production host is proven to call them before retrieval/injection.
known_problems.next_action: Continue with the one host-neutral adapter defined in PROJECT-BRAIN/NEXT-STEP.md.

known_problems.summary: Windows denied creation of the test symlink; the focused test exists but was skipped in this full-suite run.
known_problems.next_action: Run the same suite on a host that allows symlink creation when available.
